state.misconception_label: Believes f(x - a) translates the function up a units

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: What transformation maps the graph of \(y=f(x) \) to the graph of \( y=f(x-3) \). I got Translation by vector
\(
\left[\begin{array}{l}
0 \\
3
\end{array}\right]
\) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The correct transformation for \(y=f(x-3)\) is a translation to the right by 3 units, not up. Remember, when dealing with function transformations, the value inside the function affects the horizontal direction. So, the correct translation vector is \([\begin{array}{l} 3 \\ 0 \end{array}]\). Keep in mind the direction of the translation when working on similar problems in the future.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, I see! So when it’s \(f(x - a)\), it actually moves the graph to the right by \(a\) units instead of up. That’s a bit confusing! What about when it’s \(f(x + a)\)? Does that mean it moves left?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: When the function is \(f(x + a)\), it actually moves the graph to the left by \(a\) units, not up. Remember, the value inside the function affects the horizontal direction of the graph. Keep practicing with different transformations to strengthen your understanding.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get it now! So, \(f(x - a)\) moves the graph to the right and \(f(x + a)\) moves it to the left. But what about when we have something like \(f(x) + b\)? Does that move the graph up or down? I'm still a bit confused about how the outside part works!

score.justification_pass1: The teacher correctly states the right answers but simply tells the student what to remember rather than engaging with why the misconception occurred or prompting the student to reason through it, resulting in the student memorizing rules without understanding (as evidenced by their continued confusion about vertical transformations in Turn 4).
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently provides explicit procedural rules (e.g., 'the value inside the function affects the horizontal direction'), gives direct corrective feedback on the student's error (correcting the translation vector from [0,3] to [3,0]), and clearly states the procedures for different transformation types throughout the dialogue.
